description: Read the spending budget pay_service spends from: its cap, what has been spent, what remains, how many payments were made (and the limit, if any), and when it expires. Reading costs nothing and charges nothing. Use it whenever the human asks how much is left, or before a run of paid calls. Money is in CENTS: `capCents` is whole cents; `spentCents` and `remainingCents` can carry up to four decimals because the budget is charged per call at 1/10,000 of a cent (e.g. `"1.632"` = 1.632¢), and `spentCents + remainingCents = capCents` while the budget is within its cap. Tell the human `message` as it stands and never substitute a figure of your own: the budget includes routing fees and rounding, so adding up your calls will not match it. With no `delegationId` it reads the budget pay_service would use; that only includes budgets that can still pay, so `{"status":"no_active_delegation"}` also covers a budget that ran out or expired — pass the `delegationId` from an earlier pay_service result to read that one anyway. On a deployment that reports it, `spentByDeliveryStatusCents` splits the spend by what each payment delivered (`delivered`, `charged_not_delivered`, `charged_unconfirmed`, `not_charged`, `not_delivered`, `pending`, the `deliveryStatus` values list_payments uses), and `unattributedSpentCents` is spend no payment record itemizes; a non-zero `charged_not_delivered` is what was spent on calls that delivered nothing although the merchant charged (the merchant charge plus any routing fee not given back), so tell the human. `not_delivered` is held for calls the merchant answered with an error: not a confirmed charge; the reserve stays held until reconciliation decides whether the merchant charged after confirmed cancellation or authorization expiry (an older deployment reports it inside `pending`). `lockedInChannels`, when present, is money the wallet this budget pays from has deposited into payment channels with merchants that charge per call (per token, as in wallet_balance). It is that WALLET's total, shared by every budget paying from it, not a figure of this budget's own: it is NOT spent and NOT charged to this budget, it can pay further calls only to the merchant holding each channel, and what is unused comes back to that wallet when the channel closes, after 15 minutes without use; `message` then says so. An empty list means nothing is locked; `null` means it could not be read, and `message` then says that too. `sessionChannels`, when present, is the history behind that: each payment channel this budget used, newest first, with the `merchant`, its `status`, what was deposited (`deposit`, or `depositAtomic` in raw units when `symbol` is null), what came back (`refund`, null until the channel has closed and the refund is confirmed) and `openedAt`/`closedAt`. It is what explains money leaving the wallet and coming back when no payment shows it: a payment record carries one call's price, never the deposit. `sharedWithOtherBudgets` means the wallet's channel also served another budget, so its figures are not this budget's alone, and `depositConfirmed: false` means the open is not confirmed, so the deposit may not have landed. `sessionChannelsTruncated: true` means the list holds only the newest channels and older ones exist; `message` then says so. An empty list means none was used; `null` means it could not be read, and `message` then says so. Absent means this reader cannot see them: a budget owned by someone else, or an older deployment. Inventory fields `creditsCoverage` and `creditsCoverageMessage` describe public catalog eligibility, even when this caller has no subscription access or credit consent. Relay the message when present; absent means unavailable, never zero. A get_service endpoint carries `subscription` when credits can pay it. When you have a Nevermined Subscription the result also carries `subscription` (`creditsLeft`, a digit string of every unexpired credit; `resetsAt`, when the allowance expires and, unless `cancelAtPeriodEnd`, the next period's is granted; `status`, `suspended` and `plan`) and `subscriptionMessage` to relay as it stands; `subscription.subscribed: false` means none. Whether or not you subscribe, it also carries `credits` (`null`: could not be read, which is not the same as none): `total`, `spendable` (what can pay a call now), `parts` (`kind` allowance | welcome | topup | sla, `credits`, `expiresAt` — null never expires — and `frozen`: null, `renewal_overdue` for allowance credits frozen until a renewal payment goes through, `dispute` for every credit while a card dispute holds them) and `nextExpiry`, with `creditsMessage` to relay as it stands. Every amount is a digit string. Never count credits yourself. Requires your Nevermined API key on the Authorization header.

delegationId.description: A specific delegation to read (every paid pay_service result carries one). Omit it to read the budget pay_service spends by default.
